title: Session SLA Flexing and Contract Scenarios PRD
author: Lena Park
summary: Define product requirements for a dynamic Session SLA Flexing feature that lets commercial teams configure per-tenant SLA targets, automatic crediting, and contract scenarios (burst insurance, negotiated latency windows). The feature ties runtime telemetry, model variants, and billing adjustments into a single, auditable contract flow.
background: Enterprise customers increasingly request bespoke SLA windows tied to price or reserved capacity. Current offerings (standard latency SLOs + dedicated reservations) are rigid: they don't allow short-term temporary SLA relaxations, automated crediting, or contract-driven microburst insurance. This PRD proposes a productized flow that combines runtime enforcement, legal contract parameters, and billing automation to support flexible SLAs tied to session behavior.
goals: 1) Provide an API and Console UX for sales to create negotiated SLA bundles (time-bounded, per-route, per-model) that map to runtime routing and billing. 2) Automate crediting when negotiated SLOs are missed (calculated per-contract rules). 3) Enable short-term SLA relaxations ("microburst insurance") that allow customers to pay for guaranteed burst capacity with different latency multipliers. 4) Ensure full telemetry lineage so every bill adjustment and credit is traceable to runtime events.
non_goals: 1) This PRD does not replace long-term Dedicated capacity contracts. 2) Not implementing automated legal e-signing or external contract systems (integration is optional). 3) Not covering per-token quality guarantees (that remains in fidelity/accuracy docs).
detailed_requirements:
User stories and requirements:

- As a Sales/Account Manager, I want to define a "Negotiated SLA Bundle" with parameters: target SLO (latency p95), time window, covered routes, covered model variants, credit rules, and price multiplier.
- As a Tenant Admin, I want to view active negotiated SLAs, anticipated credits if SLOs fail, and simulate the contract impact on billing for a range of traffic shapes.
- As the Runtime, the system must: 1) tag incoming requests that are governed by an active negotiated SLA, 2) enforce routing preference to meet the negotiated SLO (preferred region, prewarming), 3) emit telemetry events with contract_id, route, model_variant, request_latency_ms, and success/fail flags.
- As Billing, I want an automated reconciler that consumes contract_id-tagged telemetry and emits credit transactions or invoices against the customer's account on a daily cadence.

Minimum product-level acceptance criteria (high level):
- Negotiated SLA Bundles can be created via Console and API.
- Runtime consistently emits contract-affiliated telemetry with <1% loss.
- Billing reconciler runs and posts credits within 48 hours of covered period end.
- Simulation tool forecasts cost and credit delta with error <10% for typical tenant traffic shapes.
api_spec:
Create Negotiated SLA (POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/negotiated_slas) payload example:

{
  "name": "Microburst Insurance - Q3 Renewal",
  "routes": ["/v1/chat", "/v1/generate"],
  "model_variants": ["redwood-4x-f16", "redwood-4x-q4"],
  "slo_target": { "metric": "latency_ms_p95", "threshold_ms": 250 },
  "time_window": { "start": "2029-07-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2029-09-30T23:59:59Z" },
  "burst_capacity_units": 1200,
  "price_multiplier": 1.25,
  "credit_policy": { "per_violation_credit_usd": 100, "daily_cap_usd": 10000 },
  "owner": "sales:acct-1234"
}

API responses include contract_id and an initial simulation score. Console will show a preview and require explicit "acknowledge risk" from the customer admin for higher-than-standard multipliers.
sla_definitions:
SLO and evaluation rules (applied per contract):

- Primary latency SLO: latency_ms_p95 < threshold_ms per covered route and model_variant.
- Evaluation window: daily sliding window and monthly aggregate for billing.
- Violation condition: if daily p95 > threshold_ms for covered route -> emit a violation event.
- Violation severity tiers:
  - Tier 1: daily p95 exceeds threshold by 0-20% (per_violation_credit_usd applied).
  - Tier 2: daily p95 exceeds threshold by 20-50% (2x per_violation_credit_usd applied).
  - Tier 3: daily p95 exceeds threshold by >50% (3x per_violation_credit_usd + automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant for remainder of day).

- SLO soft-fail window: the first 3 violations in a 30-day rolling window are eligible for automatic crediting; subsequent violations require account owner review and manual escalation.
pricing_logic_table:
| Scenario | Price Multiplier | Billing Action | Credit Action |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Standard (no negotiated SLA) | 1.00 | standard per-token billing | none |
| Negotiated SLA active, SLO met | negotiated multiplier (e.g., 1.25) | applied | none |
| Negotiated SLA active, single-day violation (Tier 1) | negotiated multiplier | applied | per_violation_credit_usd refunded |
| Negotiated SLA active, Tier 3 violation | negotiated multiplier | applied for usage before violation detection, then automatic reroute | per_violation_credit_usd * 3 + temporary discount on next billing cycle |
| Microburst insurance consumed (burst capacity used) | negotiated multiplier + burst surcharge | applied (burst units consumed) | none |
simulation_and_console_requirements:
Console: New 'Negotiated SLAs' page under Tenant -> Consumption with:
- List of active/past negotiated SLAs with contract_id, status, effective dates, expected monthly spend delta.
- Simulation widget where admin can upload or select traffic shapes (percentiles of session length, tokens per request, route mix) and preview expected cost and credit exposure.
- Action button for Sales to propose, with prefilled negotiation template including recommended price_multiplier and burst_capacity_units (computed by Optimize heuristics).

Simulation accuracy goals: for 95th-percentile typical traffic shapes, forecasted credit exposure must be within +/-10% of observed outcome over 30-day run-in tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end flow test: create negotiated SLA via API -> tag requests in runtime -> produce daily telemetry -> billing posts credits. Verified in staging with two tenants.
2) Telemetry completeness: >=99% of covered requests must contain contract_id tag and route/model_variant metadata.
3) Billing correctness: sample set of 500 violations in staging reconciler results in expected credit amounts (no mismatches).
4) UX: Console simulation and contract creation flows validated by Sales (sign-off from reviewers).
5) Security: contract metadata encrypted at rest and ACLed; only tenant admins and sales roles can propose or approve negotiated SLAs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Labs) - 2029-06: Build simulation prototype, add contract_id tagging to runtime for a shadow traffic slice. Owners: Eng Runtime (Miguel Reyes), Product (Lena Park).

Phase 1 (Beta customers) - 2029-07 to 2029-09: Select 3 enterprise customers (one regulated, one high-throughput, one marketplace) for closed beta. Enable Console UI and API write access. Run reconciler daily in dry-run mode. Owners: Customer Success + Eng Platform.

Phase 2 (Open Beta) - 2029-10: Open to customers on request; automatic crediting enabled, billing posts credits but flagged for review. Provide playbook for Sales and Finance.

Phase 3 (General Availability) - 2029-12: GA after three-month stability window and documented runbook. Auto reconciliation enabled by default for negotiated SLAs.

Rollback: If reconciler miscredits >0.5% of events in production over a 7-day window, revert to dry-run and alert product + finance oncall.

Operational runbooks and runbook links: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/negotiated-sla-reconciler-runbook.json
telemetry_and_metrics:
Telemetry fields emitted per request: contract_id, contract_version, route, model_variant, region, request_latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, decision_path (preferred_fallback|fallback_used|routed_to_dedicated), timestamp.

Key metrics:
- contract_violations_daily_count (by contract_id)
- contract_p95_latency_ms (by contract_id, route, model_variant)
- contract_credit_amount_usd (daily)
- simulation_forecast_error_pct (observed vs forecast)
- reconciler_success_rate_pct

SLOs for product reliability:
- reconciler availability: 99.9% monthly
- telemetry ingestion delay: median <30s, 99th <3m
- billing posting latency: credits posted within 48 hours of covered period end

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-crediting due to telemetry gaps. Mitigation: Require >=99% telemetry completeness before auto-crediting; otherwise keep reconciler in manual review.
Risk: Customers use negotiated SLAs to game routing (force high-cost variants). Mitigation: Audit trail and pricing caps; require Sales approval for multipliers >1.5x.
Risk: Complexity in billing reconciliation. Mitigation: Start with small beta customer set and run reconciler in dry-run with detailed reports for Finance before switching to auto-crediting.
